audit_scope.description: This batch primarily covers EL logic: EVM precompiles (EIP-196 EC operations), EVM control flow (JUMP/JUMPI/STOP), KECCAK256 hashing, difficulty bomb delay (EIP-2384/Muir Glacier), hard fork activation (EIP-609 Byzantium), no-ether transactions (EIP-7768), batched wallet calls (EIP-5792), empty account prohibition (EIP-7523), and the EIP governance process (EIP-1).

trusted_external_entities.name: Network Peer via P2P (devp2p)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peer nodes communicate over unauthenticated P2P network. Any node can join and send arbitrary blocks or transactions. Eclipse attacks, invalid block injection, and DoS are all possible. Relevant to EIP-2384 (difficulty validation of received blocks), EIP-609 (fork rule enforcement for peer blocks), and Muir Glacier (block header validation).

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Producer/Miner via P2P
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Block producers submit blocks containing difficulty values and transactions. Blocks must be fully validated including difficulty calculation (EIP-2384), fork rules (EIP-609), and state transition correctness. Miners are economically incentivized but not trusted.

trusted_external_entities.name: User via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Users submit transactions via public JSON-RPC. No authentication required. Transactions may be malformed, exploit gas pricing, or attempt resource exhaustion. Relevant to EIP-7768 (zero-balance transaction submission) and general transaction lifecycle.

trusted_external_entities.name: DApp via Wallet JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Decentralized applications interact with wallets via JSON-RPC. DApps are unauthenticated web applications that may attempt fingerprinting (wallet_getCapabilities), submit malformed batched calls, or exploit atomicity assumptions. Relevant to EIP-5792.

trusted_external_entities.name: Wallet User via UI
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Human users approve or reject transactions in wallet UIs. While they are the intended operators, they may not understand atomicity implications or may be socially engineered. Relevant to EIP-5792 batch approval flows.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Proposer Service via offchain API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: In EIP-7768, block proposers evaluate and fund zero-balance transactions. Proposers could front-run user transactions, manipulate execution context, or refuse service. The proposer-user relationship is adversarial by default.

trusted_external_entities.name: Consensus Layer via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The CL communicates with the EL via JWT-authenticated Engine API. While the channel is authenticated, payload content (block data, fork choice state) must still be validated by the EL. Relevant as a top-down archetypal attack vector for the EL.

trusted_external_entities.name: MEV-Boost Relay via external API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Top-down archetypal threat: external MEV relay services provide block templates. They could provide censored, invalid, or manipulated block content. No protocol-level authentication.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full block header validation required including difficulty calculation (with bomb delay offset per EIP-2384), fork rule enforcement (EIP-609), and parent chain verification. Reject blocks with mismatched difficulty.

Complete block validation: difficulty must match expected calculation, state root must be correct after execution, all transactions must be valid, and empty account invariant (EIP-7523) must hold post-merge.
Full transaction validation: signature verification, nonce ordering, gas limit checks, balance sufficiency (or zero-balance handling per EIP-7768). Rate limiting for DoS protection.
Request schema validation, chain ID verification, capability checks, atomicity enforcement, bundle size limits, and duplicate ID detection. Fingerprinting protection for wallet_getCapabilities.
Wallet must clearly present call details and atomicity guarantees. User rejection must halt entire batch. No calls should execute without explicit approval.
Two-phase simulation with rollback required. Consideration consistency must be verified between runs. Business logic must protect against griefing. User transactions must not be manipulated.

JWT authentication validates channel identity. EL must independently validate all payload content: block structure, transaction validity, state transitions, and gas accounting. Authentication does not imply content trust.
Full validation of block templates. No trust in relay-provided ordering, inclusion, or exclusion of transactions. Block must pass all consensus and execution validation.
